This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short "the Act of 1988") has been filed by the appellants/claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 18.04.2017 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, (for short "learned Tribunal") Bemetara,

sentences.text: Facts of the case in brief are that the appellants/claimants filed application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as MV Act), claiming compensation on account of death of Lekhram Yadav and Rajesh (father and son) in an accident that took place on 03.06.2016 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle truck bearing No. CG 12C 3956 by respondent No.1/driver and owner and insured with respondent No.2.
The claim application was filed inter alia
pleading

that on the date of incident i.e. 03.06.2016 deceased Lekhram @ Lakhram and Rajesh were riding on a motorcycle bearing No. CG 25 8977 and was going to village Sargaon from village Keshla to buy stone grits.
As they reached near Sargaon, the offending vehicle driven rashly and negligently by respondent No.1 dashed the motor cycle as a result of which both of them died on the spot.
The motor cycle was driven by Rajesh and deceased Lekhram @ lakram was a pillion rider.
The accident was reported to the police station Sargaon upon which Crime No. 159/16 was registered and after due investigation the charge sheet was also filed.
The total compensation of Rs. 55,60,000/- was claimed on account of both the deaths.

The deceased was aged about 42 years and he was a Contractor and earning Rs. 1200/- per day and so far as Rajesh is concerned, he was educated up to 10th Class and he would have definitely earned and helped the parents.

The application was registered by the respondents on various ground and the learned Tribunal framed issues on the basis of the above pleadings and decided the same in favour of the appellants/claimants.
Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32675 3.

Shri Amit Kumar Sahu, learned counsel for the appellants argued that the income has been wrongly taken by the Tribunal, future prospect has not been awarded and amount under all other heads is also on the lower side.

Learned counsel for the respoondent No.2 supports the award and submits that no documentary evidence to suggest that the deceased Lekhram @ Lakhram was a Contractor neither any registration certificate nor any evidence to show that he has wroked in a particular place has been brought on record.
Therefore, the finding recorded by the Tribunal is absolutely justified.
He further submits that so far as deceased Rajesh is concerned, admittedly, he was not working and was a student therefore the award is justified.

4. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
5.

From the given facts and circumstance on record, in the light of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Pranay Sethi & others, (2017) 16 SCC 680; Sarla Verma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121 and Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanhu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, (2018)
18 SCC 130, this Court assess the compensation in the following manner for deceased Lekhram @
Lakhram.
6.

sentences.text: 7. The compensation on account of death of deceased Rajesh is assessed in the following manner:

Deceased Rajesh was aged about 20 years and was a student and therefore, taking his income as Rs. 4500/-, the yearly income would come to Rs. 54,000/- (Rs. 4,500/- x 12) and after adding 40 % future prospect, it would come to Rs. 21,600/-, after addition, it would come to Rs. 75,600/- (Rs.54000/-+Rs.21,600/-) and after deducting 1/2 it would come to Rs. 37,800/-.
Applying the multiplier of 18, it would come to Rs. 6,80,400/-.
After adding Rs. 30,000/- under other admissible heads to appellant No.1 and Rs. 1,20,000/- as filial compensation to other appellants, total compensation would come to Rs. 8,30,400/-.
After adding the total amount of compensation on account of death of Lekhram and Rajesh, the enhanced amount would come to Rs.18,90,400/-(Rs.10,60,000/- +Rs. 8,30,400/-).
The learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs. 10,32,000/- on account of both the deaths which has been enhanced to Rs.18,90,400/-.

After deducting the amount awarded,
the enhanced amount is Rs. 8,58,400/-.

This enhanced amount of Rs. 8,58,400/-
shall be paid to the appellants/claimants which shall carry interest @ 6% from the date of claim application till its realization.
After the amount is deposited, Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:32675 Rs.50,000/- each shall be paid to appellants No.2 & 3.
Rs . 7,00,000/- shall be invested in the name of appellant No.1/wife in a fixed deposit in a Nationalized Bank for a period of two years.
Remaining amount be paid to appellant No.1/wife through bank transaction/account payee cheque.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced amount with interest within a period of 60 days.
8. Appeal is thus allowed in part.
